# Loment 0.1.4.5

Three things were announced in
[`v0.1.4.5-pre`](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/releases/tag/v0.1.4.5-pre) while they were still
being built; they are in this release, along with the fixes that accumulated since 0.1.4.

This is not an exhaustive changelog — the issue and pull-request numbers below are the index.

## Install

| Asset | |
|---|---|
| `loment-0.1.4.5-linux-x64.tar.gz` | Linux x86-64. Unpack anywhere; `bin/loment` is the launcher. |
| `loment-0.1.4.5-windows-x64.zip` | Windows x86-64. Unzip and run `install.cmd`. |
| `loment-0.1.4.5-windows-x64-setup.exe` | Windows x86-64, self-extracting. Double-click. |
| `loment-skill.zip` | The agent guide (`SKILL.md`) on its own, for people who want only that. |
| `SHA256SUMS` | Checksums. The installers verify the payload against this before copying anything. |

Installing and running needs **no Python, no clang and no WSL** — the package is native binaries plus
the standard library. `loment run hello.lomt` and you are done.

---

## New

### LomentGC — reclamation as a ladder

Reclamation in Loment is not one algorithm over one heap. Every `alloc` site is assigned, at compile
time, to one rung of a ladder, and *how much of this program's memory the collector is responsible
for* is a **number carried in the artifact**:

| Rung | What it does |
|---|---|
| `L0` | static promotion — a provably non-escaping allocation never reaches the heap at all |
| `L1` | last-use — the allocator front is returned right after the final use |
| `L2` | block epochs — a loop body, or either arm of an `if`, that allocates and drops returns its whole region at once |
| `L3` | mark-sweep with precise roots, triggered by bytes allocated |

All four rungs are implemented **twice** — the reference compiler (`tools/lomentc.py`) and the
self-hosted one (`loment/selfhost/`) — and the two must agree byte for byte (#109, #110, #143, #157).
The tiers `choose gc_manual` / `choose gc_auto` / `choose gc_auto_alpha` select how far down the
ladder a unit is allowed to go. Potato **v10** carries `gc_ladder` = `{l0, l1, l2, l3, total_sites}`,
and **two independent validators** check the arithmetic (`l0 + l1 + l2 + l3 == total_sites`) without
reading a single line of source (#172).

The `gc_auto_alpha` policy is no longer one fixed threshold: it follows the **live set** (#200) and
collects **generationally** — a 1024-entry card table, a write barrier at every `store8` site, and
`minor` / `major` levels (#230). The difference that matters between the tiers is not throughput but
the **ceiling**: on `loment/examples/gc_heap/` — the repository's first program that really builds on
the heap (#264) — the same linked-list walk runs to completion under `gc_auto` and `gc_auto_alpha`
and exhausts the arena under `gc_manual`. Numbers in [docs/210](docs/210-loment-gc-design.md) §7.

### Networking, on both targets

The same `.lomt` source opens a socket on Linux **and** on Windows, from the same output bytes. On
ELF the calls are the Linux syscalls directly; on PE the runtime dispatches **29 syscall numbers** —
eight for files and processes, and the whole network surface through `ws2_32`: the sockets plus
`poll`, `select`, `sendmsg` / `recvmsg`, `socketpair` and `epoll_*` (#191 and the batches in
[docs/217](docs/217-loment-socket-parity.md)). As of this release **no networking syscall is left
unimplemented** on either target. `syscall7` fills all six argument registers, so address-carrying
UDP — `sendto` / `recvfrom`, where the sixth argument is the `socklen_t` — is writable in the
language (#199). `tools/loment_pe_test.py` walks the whole surface by having a program connect to
itself.

### lompi, the package manager

`lompi` moves to **0.2.0 Alpha** and **fetches by itself**: `lompi fetch` reads the registry over a
raw socket instead of printing a `git clone` for you to run (#267). What it cannot do is HTTPS or
hostnames — there is no TLS and no resolver in the toolchain, so `http://` with an IPv4 literal is
the whole fetchable surface ([docs/236](docs/236-lompi-020-network.md)). Along the way the store
argument became optional, instance identity stopped re-reading the store, and `--opt` reached the
packaging path (#183, #188).

### Two smaller features

- **`register <name> { ... }`** — declare a `loment` subcommand from source instead of hand-placing
  a `loment-<name>` executable on `PATH` (#208).
- **The escape hatch, end to end** — `loment build --opt`, a pre-optimized kernel object, and
  `lompi obj`, for the cases where the native toolchain's lack of an optimizer is the thing in your
  way ([docs/212](docs/212-loment-offload.md), #179, #195).

## Fix

- **The Windows installer works.** ([#117](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/issues/117)) — 0.1.4's
  self-extracting `setup.exe` unpacked and exited having installed nothing: it launched `install.cmd`
  by bare file name, and where `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath` is set, `cmd` cannot resolve
  that. The launch command now carries the unpack directory. **The 0.1.4 asset itself is not being
  rebuilt** — that would change the bytes under a version number already in the wild — so 0.1.4 users
  should stay on the `zip` until they move here.
- **The installers now name a shadowing `lompi` / `loment`.** They only ever *append* to `PATH`
  (deliberately: an installer should not reorder a machine it does not own), so a copy installed
  earlier by hand wins silently — you type `lompi version` and get the older build with nothing
  explaining why. Both scripts now resolve the names after installing and print the path that is
  actually in front, without removing it.
- **`lomelf` can link an L0-promoted product.** An alloca used as a plain SSA value was not
  recognised, so a unit whose `alloc` sites were all promoted to the stack could not be linked at all
  ([#239](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/issues/239), #257). The same fix moved the write barrier
  to follow "does this unit need a heap", which had been emitting a reference to an arena that
  L0-promotion had removed.
- **Two IR bugs that made array-subscript artifacts invalid LLVM** (#177), and a release-manifest
  ordering bug that made every pull request look conflicted (#138).
- **Entry points are correctly aligned**: `stackrealign` is now emitted on `_start`, whose stack is 8
  bytes off the SysV convention (#206). Binary operators are typed by the expected type rather than
  by their operands (#204), and `loment fmt` refuses a file written in a non-native surface grammar
  instead of destroying it (#115, #203).
- **The surface-grammar translators, in batches.** About thirty issues fixed in the C, Python and
  other `choose write grammar` paths — silent drops, silently-wrong values, and files that failed to
  compile with a generic error instead of saying what was unsupported: the issues are #74,
  #115–#137 and #145–#155, and one language server crash (#142); the batches that fixed them are
  #171, #180 and #201. ([docs/211](docs/211-c-surface-grammar-sweep.md) is how they were found: a
  pure-Loment project written in each surface grammar.)
- **Two flaky criteria were made deterministic** (#190, #261); flaky checks turn unrelated pull
  requests red and cost every contributor time.

---

## What else

**Not in this release.**

- **`choose hosted`** — the dimension for artifacts that link real libc and shared libraries — is
  refused by a release build, by name ([docs/222](docs/222-lompi-020-foreign-libs.md) sec 4.5,
  [docs/219](docs/219-world-ports.md) sec 8c, #207, #258). The capability is in the development
  channel; calling libc from a 0.1.4.5 build is not offered.
- **The `vm` dimension** is in `main` and is **refused by a release build** the same way — it is a
  gate, not a feature, and an extension module's bytecode does not exist yet.
- **The development side is not self-hosted.** The toolchain compiles and runs with no Python at run
  time, but the reference implementation (`tools/lomentc.py` and friends) and the Python test suites
  are still in the repository ([docs/189](docs/189-full-selfhosting.md)). "The repository contains
  only Loment" is not yet true.
- **There is no networking library and no admission gate.** `std` has no `net` module — you write the
  syscalls yourself — and a unit that declares `excluded "network: ..."` is not stopped from calling
  `socket`, because the capability check compares domain names and never looks at behaviour
  ([docs/218](docs/218-loment-net-admission.md)).

**Known bugs, still open.** The ones most likely to be met, with their issue numbers:

- [#164](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/issues/164) — `free` checks neither ownership nor
  double-free, so freeing twice puts one region both at the frontier and on the free list, and two
  live allocations alias. Also [#165](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/issues/165): the Rust
  backend lowers `free` to a no-op.
- [#265](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/issues/265) — a function with 11 or more parameters makes
  the self-hosted compiler die with `SIGILL`, silently, where the reference implementation accepts it.
- [#163](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/issues/163) — `lompi` truncates any source file larger
  than 256 KiB, and the content-hash identity covers only the truncated part.
- [#226](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/issues/226) — a flat expression of ~250 terms makes
  `check` die with a `RecursionError` instead of a diagnostic.
- [#149](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/issues/149) — `check` does not check the bodies of
  modules brought in by `use`, so a library can ship with a body type error and every consumer checks
  clean. [#139](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/issues/139): two files that declare the same
  module name pass `check` and then produce IR with two `define i32 @f`.
- [#262](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/issues/262) — both language servers ignore the
  `choose write grammar` declaration, so a valid file in a non-native grammar reports false
  diagnostics.
- [#237](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/issues/237),
  [#236](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/issues/236),
  [#235](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/issues/235),
  [#234](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/issues/234),
  [#218](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/issues/218) — the same program can compute different
  numbers depending on which surface grammar it is written in: integer widths, block scope, and a
  `bool` parameter that cannot be called.
- [#205](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/issues/205),
  [#224](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/issues/224) — two places where the reference compiler
  emits invalid or wrongly-typed LLVM (pointer comparison; `bool` arithmetic).
- [#160](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/issues/160)–[#162](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/issues/162),
  [#167](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/issues/167),
  [#168](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/issues/168),
  [#159](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/issues/159),
  [#166](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/issues/166) — capability-audit bounds, unchecked input
  parsing in `lomelf` and `lomt_from.py`, dependency paths with no containment check, and a VS Code
  extension that declares no untrusted-workspace capability.
- [#266](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/issues/266) — one networking criterion is still flaky.

**Two version numbers inside `lompi`.** The package manager reports `lompi 0.2.0`; the standard
library it ships and installs is the bundle stamped `0.1.0` (`lompi list` shows `std 0.1.0` and
`host 0.1.0`). They are different axes — the library bundle did not change in this release — but the
two numbers sitting next to each other is a fair thing to trip over ([docs/170](docs/170-loment-lompi-bundling.md)).

**The language surface is frozen** ([docs/158](docs/158-loment-freeze.md) says what changing it
costs); the implementation is not. What 0.1.4 included, listed item by item and audited, is in
[docs/202](docs/202-loment-014-release-gate.md).
